s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal pain with progressive renal failure and obstructive uropathy
salient_findings: Confluent retroperitoneal soft-tissue mass encasing surrounding vessels
Bilateral hydronephrosis with extrinsic compression and medial deviation of the ureters
Progressively worsening epigastric pain with nausea, vomiting, and decreased urine output
key_facts: 50-year-old woman with hypertension and COPD
Initial presentation with lower abdominal pain and decreased bowel movements
Diagnosed with constipation, then presumed diverticulitis
Abdominal CT revealed a confluent retroperitoneal soft-tissue mass
HIDA scan confirmed cholecystitis, and she underwent cholecystectomy
Post-surgery, she had worsening epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting, and decreased urine output
Denies fevers, chills, dysuria, or GI bleeding
Slight epigastric tenderness without guarding on exam
Elevated creatinine (8.18 mg/dL) and hyperkalemia (5.1 mEq/L)
Mild bilateral hydronephrosis on renal ultrasound
Retrograde pyelogram showed bilateral hydronephrosis with extrinsic compression and medial deviation of the ureters
Ureteral stents placed, relieving obstruction and improving renal function

shortlist.label: Retroperitoneal fibrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Confluent retroperitoneal soft-tissue mass and bilateral hydronephrosis with extrinsic compression

shortlist.label: Retroperitoneal sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive renal failure and obstructive uropathy with a soft-tissue mass

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Retroperitoneal mass and obstructive uropathy, lymphoma can cause renal failure

shortlist.label: Metastatic cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Retroperitoneal mass and obstructive uropathy, metastatic cancer can cause renal failure

shortlist.label: Retroperitoneal lymph node metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: Retroperitoneal mass and obstructive uropathy, lymph node metastasis can cause renal failure

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a confluent retroperitoneal soft-tissue mass, bilateral hydronephrosis, and extrinsic compression of the ureters is most consistent with retroperitoneal fibrosis, which can cause ureteral obstruction and renal impairment.

rejected.label: Retroperitoneal sarcoma
rejected.why: While a retroperitoneal sarcoma could cause a mass and obstruction, the patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more suggestive of a fibrotic process.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Lymphoma could cause a retroperitoneal mass, but the patient's lack of systemic symptoms such as fevers, chills, and weight loss makes this less likely.

rejected.label: Metastatic cancer
rejected.why: There is no clear primary malignancy identified, and the patient's symptoms and imaging findings are not typical for metastatic disease.

rejected.label: Retroperitoneal lymph node metastasis
rejected.why: Similar to metastatic cancer, there is no clear primary malignancy identified, and the patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more suggestive of a primary retroperitoneal process.
